prompt: Why does Kwale's cut set end at atmospheric residue?
options: Neither Kwale crude carries a TBP point above 650 F, so nothing heavier than that can be cut.
The Kwale refinery has no vacuum unit, so it has nowhere to split the heavy end further.
The engine closes every cut set with an open residue cut, so no refinery's set can split it.
A cut set that splits the residue cannot close on a two crude blend, so the engine joins it.
explanation: The course gives the reason in one line: the Kwale refinery has no vacuum unit, so its cut set ends at atmospheric residue. Kwale draws its own cut points.

prompt: What is the Kwale blend's Naphtha yield on Kwale's cut set?
options: 20.4189 volume percent, the two crudes' naphtha yields weighted by mass fraction.
22.6185 volume percent, the same blend's naphtha on the studio's default cuts.
24.2512 volume percent, the naphtha yield of Kwale Light, which holds 55 of the barrels.
20.5591 volume percent, from cutYields on the blend's own curve.
explanation: Kwale's naphtha runs from 90 F to 330 F. 20.4189 is the mass-weighted reading, 22.6185 is the default set's naphtha from 90 F to 350 F, and 24.2512 is Kwale Light alone.

prompt: On Kwale's cuts, what Diesel / AGO figures does the course print for the Kwale blend by cutYields on its curve, by blendOnVolume and by blendOnMass?
explanation: The Diesel / AGO row reads 19.3849 for the blend by cutYields, 19.3849 volume-weighted from the two crudes, a difference of 0.0000, and 19.4040 mass-weighted from the two crudes. 16.9510 is the blend's Diesel / Gasoil on the studio's default cuts.

prompt: On the Kwale blend, which figure is the engine's Atmospheric residue yield, and which is the mass-weighted reading beside it?
options: 43.2685 is the yield; 43.0526 is the crudes' yields weighted by volume (blendOnVolume).
43.0526 is the yield; 43.2685 is the residue on the studio's default cuts, where it runs to vacuum residue.
43.0526 is the yield; 43.2685 is the two crudes' yields weighted by mass fraction (blendOnMass).
Both are yields: 43.0526 is on volume for the barrels, 43.2685 on mass for pricing by the tonne.
explanation: cutYields returns each cut's yield in volume percent, and the engine's column is the blend by cutYields on its own curve. 43.2685 sits in the column mass-weighted from the two crudes (blendOnMass). The Kwale blend's Vacuum residue on the default cuts is 16.3586.

prompt: Ughelli Medium's own LPG / Light ends yield on Kwale's cuts is 0.0000. Why?
options: Its curve starts at 0 percent at 90 F, which is exactly where Kwale's LPG cut ends.
Its assay carries no light ends, so the engine enters a zero below any crude's first point, whatever percent that point is at.
The engine drops a crude's LPG cut when its API is below the blend API of 33.1219.
Its LPG / Light ends yield is unknown, and the engine prints an unknown yield as zero.
explanation: None of Ughelli Medium has distilled by the top of that cut. Kwale Light starts at 75 F and has 1.3043 percent by 90 F, and the blend's 0.7174 carries only Kwale Light's share.

prompt: What does Closes: true on the Kwale blend's cut yields certify?
options: The yields were scaled by the engine to total 100.0000, so every barrel is counted exactly once.
The blend's yields match the volume-weighted crude yields on every row with a difference of 0.0000.
Every cut in the set lies wholly inside the stretch of temperature both crudes measured.
Every cut has a yield, and together the yields sum to 100.0000, inside the closing tolerance.
explanation: Closing needs a yield for every cut and a total inside the engine's closing tolerance of 100 percent, and the total is not normalised. The 0.0000 difference column is a separate reading of the two routes.

prompt: The diesel end point is moved from 650 F to 700 F on the Kwale blend. What changes?
options: Diesel / AGO gains 5.0376, and the -5.0376 is spread across Kerosene / DPK and Atmospheric residue by their yields.
Diesel / AGO gains 5.0376 and Atmospheric residue changes by -5.0376, and every other cut and the total change by 0.0000.
Diesel / AGO rises to 24.4225 and the total rises by 5.0376, since the new barrels come from past the curve's end.
Diesel / AGO gains 5.0376 and Kerosene / DPK changes by -5.0376, since kerosene is diesel's neighbour on the curve.
explanation: The moved temperature is diesel's top and residue's bottom, so one quantity is added in one place and subtracted in the other. Atmospheric residue falls from 43.0526 to 38.0150.

prompt: Why does the total of the Kwale blend's cut yields change by 0.0000 when the diesel end point moves?
options: The engine normalises the total back to 100.0000 after any cut point moves.
The moved barrels are taken from the lost volume, which sits outside the total.
Moving a cut point moves barrels between two cuts and nowhere else.
The Diesel / AGO gain is small enough that the total rounds back to 100.0000.
explanation: The course prints the rule with the table: moving a cut point moves barrels between two cuts and nowhere else. Diesel / AGO changes by 5.0376, Atmospheric residue by -5.0376 and the total by 0.0000. The total is reported as it computes and is never normalised.

prompt: In the cut table, which Naphtha and Kerosene / DPK figures stand in the Kwale Light column?
options: 24.2512 and 18.1944 volume percent.
16.0465 and 13.9535 volume percent.
20.5591 and 16.2860 volume percent.
24.2512 and 13.9535 volume percent.
explanation: The Kwale Light column reads Naphtha 24.2512 and Kerosene / DPK 18.1944. Ughelli Medium's column reads 16.0465 and 13.9535, and the blend reads 20.5591 and 16.2860.

prompt: Kwale Light is blended 50 and 50 with the Ebocha partial assay and cut on Kwale's set. Why do LPG / Light ends and Naphtha come back unknown?
options: Each lies above 920 F, where the blend's curve stops, so the curve has no value at their upper bounds.
Ebocha carries no light ends, so the engine marks every cut lighter than kerosene as unknown.
Their yields fall below the engine's closing tolerance, so they are reported as unknown.
Each has a bound below 110 F, where the blend's curve starts, so the curve has no value at 90 F.
explanation: The blend's curve starts at 110 F and stops at 920 F. unknownCuts: LPG / Light ends, Naphtha.

prompt: The partial blend's curve stops at 920 F, yet Atmospheric residue gets a yield of 40.1548. Why?
options: The engine takes Ebocha as wholly distilled above 920 F for the residue cut alone, and so the cut can close.
The residue yield is the known cuts' shortfall from 100 percent, carried into the last cut so the set can close.
It has no upper bound: it runs from its lower bound of 650 F to 100 percent, and 650 F lies inside the curve.
Kwale Light is known above 920 F, so the residue is valued on Kwale Light's own residue yield of 37.3684.
explanation: A last cut with no upper bound takes everything not yet distilled at its lower bound. Kerosene / DPK, 16.9626, and Diesel / AGO, 19.2202, also sit wholly inside the curve.

prompt: What does the engine report for the cuts with a yield on the partial blend, and does it scale them?
options: They are scaled up to total 100.0000, spreading the missing barrels over the known cuts.
They total 76.3376 percent, reported as computed, with no scaling toward 100 percent.
They total 33.6742 percent, the known cuts of the Ebocha partial assay on the default set.
They total 76.3376 percent, and the engine scales them only when unknownCuts is empty.
explanation: The course prints: the cuts with a yield total 76.3376 percent, and the total is reported as it computes and is never normalised. 33.6742 belongs to the Ebocha partial assay alone on the studio's cuts.

prompt: On the Kwale Light and Ebocha blend cut on Kwale's set, what do unknownCuts and Closes read?
options: unknownCuts: LPG / Light ends, Naphtha. Closes: false.
unknownCuts: LPG / Light ends, Naphtha. Closes: true.
unknownCuts: Atmospheric residue. Closes: false.
unknownCuts: LPG / Light ends, Naphtha, Vacuum gasoil, Vacuum residue. Closes: false.
explanation: The course prints unknownCuts: LPG / Light ends, Naphtha. Closes: false. Atmospheric residue has a yield, 40.1548, because it runs from 650 F to 100 percent. Four cuts with no yield belong to the Ebocha partial assay alone on the studio's cuts.

prompt: Kwale Light and the Ebocha partial assay are valued as a blend on the Kwale refinery's prices, costs and losses. What comes back?
options: A refusal in place of a figure, because netbackValue will not value any blend whose cut yields do not close, and it names the cuts that stopped it.
A netback of 48.3393 $/bbl with complete: true, since the missing cuts are already named in unknownCuts and a named gap leaves a valuation whole.
A netback over the three cuts it can value, with LPG / Light ends and Naphtha entered at a yield of 0.0000 and complete: true.
A netback of 48.3393 $/bbl over the cuts it can value, with unyieldedCuts naming LPG / Light ends and Naphtha and complete: false.
explanation: The course prints unyieldedCuts: LPG / Light ends, Naphtha beside the 48.3393 $/bbl, and complete: false. Both cuts keep an empty yield and an empty value.

prompt: The Kwale blend yields 0.7174 percent LPG / Light ends on Kwale's cuts and on the studio's default cuts. Why do the two tables agree on that row?
options: Light ends are fixed by the crudes' API and do not depend on where any cut point is drawn.
The engine reports the first cut of every set on the blend's own grid, whatever its bounds.
Both cut sets draw it from 0 percent to 90 F, so it is the same stretch of the same curve.
The default set is Kwale's set with a vacuum split added, so every cut it shares agrees.
explanation: Where a boundary moves, the yields on either side of it move with it: Kerosene / DPK reads 16.2860 on Kwale's cuts and Kerosene / Jet 16.6604 on the default set.
